analysis.summary: The Content Fragment Model for 'page' has undergone extensive structural changes including field node renames and modifications to reference properties, which will cause data loss and runtime errors for existing content.

bugs.title: Renaming of Content Fragment Model field nodes
bugs.lineHint: Line 53 (tab-sxiXYxUvUJ, previously _x0031_650472887391) and multiple other field nodes below it.
bugs.description: Many content fragment model field nodes (e.g., `_x0031_650472887391`, `_x0031_650472802805`) have been renamed to more descriptive names (e.g., `tab-sxiXYxUvUJ`, `language`).
bugs.risk: This is a HIGH severity functional bug. Existing content fragments created using this model will lose their data for these fields, as the underlying JCR property names used to store the content will no longer match the model's new field definitions. This will result in broken pages, empty content, and potential runtime errors when components attempt to access non-existent properties.

bugs.title: Removal of `nameSuffix` from fragment reference fields
bugs.description: The `nameSuffix="contentReference"` property has been removed from several fragment reference fields (e.g., `footerContentTag`, `banner`, `header`).
bugs.risk: This is a HIGH severity functional bug. The removal of `nameSuffix` implicitly changes the JCR property name under which existing content fragment references are stored (e.g., from `footerContentTag_contentReference` to `footerContentTag`). Consequently, existing references will become invalid, preventing linked content fragments from being resolved and displayed, leading to broken page layouts and functionality.

bugs.title: Type change for `fragmentmodelreference` attribute on single references
bugs.description: The `fragmentmodelreference` attribute for single content fragment reference fields (e.g., `footerContentTag`, `banner`) has been changed from a single string path (e.g., `"/path"`) to an array containing a single string path (e.g., `"[/path]"`).
bugs.risk: This is a HIGH severity functional bug. While standard AEM components might handle this type change gracefully, custom components or rendering logic might strictly expect a string type for this property. Passing an array where a string is expected could cause runtime type mismatch errors during content fragment resolution or in the authoring UI, leading to component failure or an inability for authors to configure fragment references.

notBugs.reason: Changes to `cq:lastModified`, `cq:lastReplicated`, etc., are system-generated and do not indicate functional bugs.
The `listOrder` property primarily affects the display order of fields in the UI. Its removal might alter the UI presentation but does not cause runtime errors or incorrect functional behavior.

Adding `translatable` attributes and standardizing boolean/array syntax (e.g., `true` to `{Boolean}true`, single validation string to array `[validation]`) are likely configuration corrections or improvements and are not expected to cause runtime errors or incorrect behavior.

The `uiSchema` defines the UI layout for the Content Fragment Model editor. While it reflects the structural changes, it's a consequence of the field renames (which are bugs) and not a primary cause of runtime errors on published pages. It primarily affects the authoring experience.
